content: Phenobarbital interacts with various drugs by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to reduced plasma levels and therapeutic effects of these drugs. Below is a detailed explanation of the interactions: 1. Flurazepam: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of flurazepam by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Fondaparinux: Phenobarbital increases the metabolism of fondaparinux, reducing its efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Fostamatinib: Phenobarbital decreases fostamatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Fruquintinib: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of fruquintinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Ganaxolone: Phenobarbital decreases ganaxolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase the ganaxolone dose without exceeding the maximum daily dose. 6. Gilteritinib: Phenobarbital reduces gilteritinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Glasdegib: Phenobarbital decreases glasdegib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 8. Heparin: Phenobarbital increases heparin metabolism, reducing its effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Hydrocodone: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases the risk of profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration unless no alternatives exist. Limit dosages and monitor closely for respiratory depression. 10. Ibrutinib: Phenobarbital reduces ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 10-fold via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Idelalisib: Avoid coadministration. 12. Infigratinib: Phenobarbital reduces infigratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Irinotecan: Phenobarbital decreases irinotecan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Isocarboxazid: Phenobarbital should not be used with isocarboxazid due to the risk of central nervous system (CNS) depression. Avoid coadministration. 15. Isosorbide Dinitrate and Mononitrate: Phenobarbital reduces their levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Istradefylline: Phenobarbital decreases istradefylline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 17. Ivabradine: Phenobarbital reduces ivabradine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 18. Ivacaftor: Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 19. Ivosidenib: Phenobarbital decreases ivosidenib plasma concentrations by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 20. Ixazomib: Phenobarbital reduces ixazomib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 21. Larotrectinib: Phenobarbital decreases larotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose and resume the prior dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer. 22. Lefamulin: Phenobarbital reduces lefamulin efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless benefits outweigh risks. 23. Lemborexant: Phenobarbital decreases lemborexant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Lenacapavir: Phenobarbital reduces lenacapavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 25. Lenolisib: Phenobarbital decreases lenolisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Letermovir: Phenobarbital reduces letermovir levels via P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration. 27. Levetiracetam: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid coadministration unless no alternatives exist. 28. Lomitapide: Phenobarbital reduces lomitapide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Lovastatin: Phenobarbital decreases lovastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Lumateperone: Phenobarbital reduces lumateperone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Lurbinectedin: Phenobarbital decreases lurbinectedin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Macimorelin: Phenobarbital may cause false-positive test results by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue strong CYP3A4 inducers before testing. 33. Macitentan: Phenobarbital reduces macitentan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 34. Mavorixafor: Phenobarbital decreases mavorixafor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Mestranol: Phenobarbital increases mestranol metabolism, potentially causing contraceptive failure. Use alternative contraception methods. 36. Methohexital: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid coadministration unless no alternatives exist. 37. Methoxyflurane: Phenobarbital increases methoxyflurane metabolism to nephrotoxic compounds. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Methylene Blue: Co-administration with belladonna alkaloids increases serotonin levels. Avoid coadministration unless necessary, and monitor for serotonergic toxicity. 39. Metoclopramide (Intranasal): Phenobarbital increases metoclopramide effects. Avoid coadministration unless necessary. 40. Midostaurin: Phenobarbital reduces midostaurin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 41. Modafinil: Phenobarbital decreases modafinil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Naldemedine: Phenobarbital reduces naldemedine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 43. Neratinib: Phenobarbital decreases neratinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 44. Netupitant/Palonosetron: Phenobarbital reduces netupitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 45. Nintedanib: Phenobarbital decreases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration. 46. Nirogacestat: Phenobarbital reduces nirogacestat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 47. Norethindrone: Phenobarbital reduces norethindrone levels, potentially causing contraceptive failure. Use alternative contraception methods. 48. Norgestrel: Phenobarbital decreases norgestrel levels, increasing the risk of contraceptive failure. Use alternative contraception methods. 49. Olanzapine/Samidorphan: Phenobarbital reduces olanzapine and samidorphan levels by approximately 50% and 75%, respectively. Avoid coadministration. 50. Olaparib: Phenobarbital decreases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 51. Oliceridine: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases sedation. Avoid coadministration unless no alternatives exist. 52. Olutasidenib: Phenobarbital reduces olutasidenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 53. Avoid coadministration. 55. Ozanimod: Phenobarbital reduces ozanimod active metabolite levels via CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 56. Palbociclib: Avoid coadministration. 57. Palovarotene: Phenobarbital reduces palovarotene levels via CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 58. Pexidartinib: Phenobarbital decreases pexidartinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless benefits outweigh risks. 63. Pralsetinib: Phenobarbital decreases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration. 64. Pretomanid: Phenobarbital reduces pretomanid levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 65. Avoid coadministration. 70. Rimegepant: Phenobarbital reduces rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 71. Avoid coadministration. 73. Rivaroxaban: Phenobarbital reduces rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 74. Rolapitant: Phenobarbital reduces rolapitant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 75. Romidepsin: Phenobarbital decreases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 76. Ropinterferon Alfa-2b: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid coadministration. 77. Selinexor: Phenobarbital may exacerbate neurological toxicities associated with selinexor. Avoid coadministration. 78. Selpercatinib: Phenobarbital reduces selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 79. Selumetinib: Phenobarbital decreases selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 80. Sildenafil: Phenobarbital reduces sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 81. Silodosin: Phenobarbital decreases silodosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 82. Simvastatin: Phenobarbital reduces simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 83. Siponimod: Phenobarbital reduces siponimod levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 84. Sirolimus: Phenobarbital decreases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 85. Sofosbuvir: Phenobarbital reduces sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration. 86. Sonidegib: Phenobarbital decreases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 87. Sorafenib: Phenobarbital reduces sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 88. Sotagliflozin: Phenobarbital reduces sotagliflozin levels via UGT1A9 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 89. Sotorasib: Phenobarbital decreases sotorasib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 90. Sparsentan: Phenobarbital reduces sparsentan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 91. Stiripentol: Phenobarbital reduces stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 92. Sufentanil: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases the risk of sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death. Avoid coadministration unless no alternatives exist. 93. Tamsulosin: Phenobarbital reduces tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 94. Tazemetostat: Phenobarbital decreases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 95. Tetracycline: Phenobarbital reduces tetracycline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 96. Tezacaftor: Phenobarbital decreases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 97. Tivozanib: Phenobarbital reduces tivozanib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 98. Tizanidine: Phenobarbital reduces tizanidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. This list highlights the significant interactions of phenobarbital with various drugs, emphasizing the need to avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies in most cases.
